A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite additions and substantial table relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning experiments measuring misalignment, coherence, and benign-task performance, including hyperparameter sweeps and GRPO results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds inoculation-prompting comparisons, on-policy interleaving results, and repeated-seed FoQA experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 adds an on-policy interleaving variant that regenerates WildGuardMix answers using the original aligned model. Section 3.1 also introduces inoculation prompting as an evaluated intervention. The proposed Interleaving+/++ scoring and refusal-filtering procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions cover Code, Legal, Medical, Security, OpSwap, FoQA, GSM8K, and the same general misalignment evaluation. On-policy answer generation retains WildGuardMix prompt and task coverage; no additional domain, language, population, or test scenario is established.

E2.justification: v3 adds inoculation prompting to the 7B and 32B misalignment comparisons and to OpSwap, FoQA, and GSM8K evaluations. It also adds on-policy interleaving to both model-scale misalignment comparisons. LDIFS remains experimentally evaluated despite disappearing from the introductory summary table.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds a controlled FoQA steering-strength sweep, while new on-policy experiments evaluate interleaving fractions from 1% to 50%. Existing splits, metrics, and training configurations are retained. However, Table 2's new on-policy rows match Table 18's 20% setting despite Section 4.3 specifying 5% for all interleaving variants.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends supplementary analysis: Tables 18 and 22 test whether model-generated safety answers improve the coherence trade-off across interleaving fractions and model sizes. Appendix F additionally investigates the strength dependence and reproducibility of the unexpected FoQA benefit from persona steering. Existing sweeps and GRPO training curves remain.

E5.justification: v3 explicitly labels the main SFT results and appendix sweeps as single-run results. Appendix F reports newly performed FoQA experiments using five seeds per setting with means and standard deviations. Three-seed mean-and-standard-deviation reporting for GRPO already existed in v2.

E6.justification: Retained numerical results are unchanged, but substantial new comparator and analysis results appear. Examples include 91.00% GSM8K accuracy for inoculation prompting, on-policy interleaving results at both model scales, and five-seed FoQA scores of 48.91±0.16 for persona steering at alpha=5 versus 40.68±0.71 without intervention.

T1.justification: Appendix E adds computational-cost assumptions and an overhead formula, Equation 10, absent from v2. Existing method equations remain unchanged. The new formula appears to reverse the fine-tuning and candidate-data sample counts relative to the stated scoring-versus-training cost calculation.

C1.justification: The abstract expands the study from four to five intervention types, and the introduction adds claims about inoculation prompting's model-size dependence and interference with narrow misalignment. The central contribution and conclusion favoring automatically selected safety interleaving remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 interprets retained Code results as evidence of transfer across distinct misalignment domains and newly identifies keyword-based refusal filtering as a limitation. Appendix F proposes reduced overfitting as a possible explanation for FoQA improvements while explicitly questioning generalization beyond the tested setup.

D1.justification: v3 documents the inoculation prompt and its integration with GRPO formatting, clarifies that the 24 evaluation questions comprise eight questions in three formats, and adds mitigation-cost details. Reported total compute changes from approximately 350 to 1000 GPU-hours, and the anonymous code link is replaced with a named GitHub repository.

R1.justification: v3 adds Tan et al. and Wichers et al. on inoculation prompting and positions that approach alongside persona steering. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata or consolidate duplicate citations, including the two Wang entries, without substantially changing research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 standardizes EMA to EM and preventative to preventive, makes local grammatical edits, and updates affiliations, publication information, and acknowledgments. It adds a cost subsection and Appendices E–F, while retaining most prose and the main narrative order.

P2.justification: The appendix displays are substantially reorganized: hyperparameter tables are grouped at the end, and GRPO figures are collected near their results. v3 adds three tables and expands existing comparisons. Table 1 replaces LDIFS with inoculation prompting; the three figures are retained, with clarification added to Figure 1's caption.

improvement.justification: The added alternatives strengthen the comparative study, and Appendix F's five-seed FoQA evidence addresses v2's uncertainty about whether persona-vector gains were noise. Explicit single-run reporting also improves transparency. These benefits are tempered by the new on-policy budget mismatch between Tables 2 and 18 and the reversed sample-count ratio in Equation 10, limiting the net quality gain.
